classifications.rationale: The President presently proclaims the trade embargo; its legal consequence arises from the proclamation itself, with paragraphs 2 and 3 defining its operation.
classifications.evidence: Hereby proclaim an embargo upon trade between the United States and Cuba

classifications.rationale: The President directly prohibits the specified imports as of the stated effective time, so the segment itself creates the legal restriction.
classifications.evidence: Hereby prohibit, effective 12:01 A.M., Eastern Standard Time, February 7, 1962, the importation into the United States

classifications.rationale: The President assigns Treasury responsibility for implementing the already-created prohibition and grants discretion to make exceptions, without dictating any particular exception.
classifications.evidence: authorize and direct the Secretary of the Treasury to carry out such prohibition

classifications.rationale: The Secretary receives discretion to determine consistency with the embargo and issue regulations as necessary; no specified later legal outcome is mandated.
classifications.evidence: to promulgate such rules and regulations as may be necessary to perform such functions

classifications.rationale: The President mandates the Secretary of Commerce to maintain through agency administration the specified legally consequential ban on all exports to Cuba.
classifications.evidence: direct the Secretary of Commerce, under the provisions of the Export Control Act of 1949, as amended

classifications.rationale: The President grants the Secretary discretionary authority over exceptions without requiring any specified exception or other legal outcome.
classifications.evidence: authorize him, under that Act, to continue, make, modify, or revoke exceptions
